title: The RBI Hopes For The Best
gist: The Reserve Bank of India held its repo rate at 5.25% with a neutral stance while most other central banks turned hawkish, a divergence it can afford because April-June activity (industrial output at a two-year high, accelerating corporate credit) held up and inflation stayed inside the 2-6% target band. The framing implies the hold is a bet that creeping inflation stays contained rather than a settled call.

insights.claim: The Reserve Bank of India left its benchmark repo rate unchanged at 5.25% and kept a neutral policy stance, declining to follow the hawkish turn taken by many other central banks.
insights.speaker: Gavekal Research
insights.so_what: A confirmed policy-rate floor at 5.25% with a neutral bias supports Indian duration and rate-sensitive equities versus EM peers that are still tightening.

insights.claim: Keeping inflation inside the 2-6% target band is what allowed India to avoid the pro-cyclical tightening that Indonesia and the Philippines were forced into.
insights.speaker: Gavekal Research
insights.so_what: Frames the trade as long India rates/equities against Indonesia and the Philippines, where policy is tightening into a slowdown; the band is the trigger to watch.
insights.quote: allowing India to avoid the pro-cyclical tightening forced upon the likes of Indonesia and the Philippines.

insights.claim: Indian inflation is steadily creeping higher even while still inside the RBI's 2-6% band, so the neutral hold is a bet that the drift stays contained rather than a settled judgment.
insights.speaker: Gavekal Research
insights.so_what: If CPI breaches 6%, the RBI would be forced into exactly the pro-cyclical tightening it has so far dodged, repricing Indian front-end rates sharply.
insights.quote: inflation—although steadily creeping higher—remained within the RBI’s target band of 2-6%

insights.claim: Indian industrial output rose at its fastest pace in more than two years in the April-June quarter, led by the electricity and manufacturing sectors.
insights.speaker: Gavekal Research
insights.so_what: Two-year-high industrial momentum argues for Indian capex, power and industrial names rather than defensives, and removes the growth excuse for near-term cuts.
insights.quote: Industrial output rose at the fastest pace in more than two years, with strong growth in the electricity and manufacturing sectors.
insights.locator: Despite multiple headwinds, India’s economy maintained

insights.claim: Indian bank credit accelerated in the April-June quarter on strong loan demand from corporates rather than households.
insights.speaker: Gavekal Research
insights.so_what: Corporate-led credit growth is the cleanest read-through to Indian bank loan books and a private capex cycle; watch it as the confirming signal for the industrial upturn.
insights.quote: Bank credit accelerated on strong demand from corporates.
insights.locator: Bank credit accelerated on strong demand

insights.claim: India's economy sustained decent momentum through April-June despite facing multiple headwinds, per Gavekal's read of the quarter.
insights.speaker: Gavekal Research
insights.so_what: Resilience-despite-headwinds is the core case for staying overweight India in EM allocations, though the teaser does not specify which headwinds.
insights.locator: Despite multiple headwinds, India’s economy maintained
